task.description: Implement §11.10.5's three signature-level changes to test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (provision_wrap/teardown_wrap split, guarded/2 and log_teardown/3 :exit widening), implement §11.10.4's post-teardown verification, then re-run the full §11.7 + §11.10.4 regression plan with real quoted output.
acceptance_criteria: provision_wrap/teardown_wrap split implemented exactly as §11.10.5 item 1 specifies
guarded/2 and log_teardown/3 widened to catch :exit per §11.10.5 items 2-3, teardown/2 itself left unwrapped
Post-teardown verification (§11.10.4 item 2) added and genuinely proves teardown ran, not merely that ExUnit did not observe a red
Full §11.7 + §11.10.4 regression plan re-run with real quoted output
mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force and mix format --check-formatted clean

result.summary:
Implemented §11.10.5's three changes exactly as specified (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex: provision_wrap/teardown_wrap split at the provisioned_tenant!/1 dispatch site; guarded/2 and log_teardown/3's trailing rescue clause both widened to `rescue _exception -> degraded/:ok catch :exit, _reason -> degraded/:ok`; teardown/2's own DROP SCHEMA/delete_all statements left unwrapped, per §11.10.3's explicit requirement). mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force and mix format --check-formatted are both clean.

While implementing §11.10.4 item 2's post-teardown verification (added to test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs as two sequenced tests using :persistent_term to hand the tenant_id/schema_name across), the verification exposed a genuine, previously-undiagnosed defect in §11.10.2's own design premise, not something my implementation introduced. Re-deriving from source rather than trusting my own first-pass green result (per core-directives.md 're-derive under the conditions the property is actually about'): I wrote my first verification test to check post-teardown state via Letflow.Repo (the ambient connection) and it passed -- but that is the WRONG connection to check from, because ExUnit checks the sandboxed connection back in (and rolls it back) via a process monitor firing on the owning test process's death, and that rollback happening is indistinguishable, from Letflow.Repo's own point of view, from a real DROP SCHEMA having run. I re-ran the same check via Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo (the genuinely separate connection teardown_wrap now routes through) and got schema_present_before_drop=false BEFORE the DROP even runs, in test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs's own pre-existing C5 test ('emits one marked teardown line naming the schema and its presence', which asserts schema_present_before_drop=true and now fails).

Root-caused with a minimal, TenantFixture-free reproduction (test/letflow/zzz_diag_test.exs, deleted after use, not left in the tree): a plain `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false` test that does `Repo.query!(CREATE SCHEMA ...)` in its own body, then in on_exit/1 tries to see that schema via a second repo (Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo). Result: the schema is NOT visible (query returns zero rows), and a follow-up direct Letflow.Repo query from inside the same on_exit/1 raises `DBConnection.OwnershipError: cannot find ownership process ... using mode :manual (Note that a connection's mode reverts to :manual if its owner terminates.)` -- confirmed from Ecto's own error text, not inferred. This establishes, from source and by direct reproduction, that DataCase.setup/1's Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo) call (test/support/data_case.ex:16) wraps EVERY test's connection in a real sandboxed (rollback-only, never-committing) transaction -- Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.checkout/2's own :sandbox option defaults to true and neither DataCase nor TenantFixture ever pass sandbox: false -- regardless of whether the pool's own mode is :auto or :manual at checkout time. {:shared, self()} mode (what async: false gets) does not change this: per Sandbox.mode/2's own moduledoc, {:shared, pid} presumes a connection 'checked out in manual mode' and shares THAT SAME wrapped transaction across allowed processes: it is still one rollback-only transaction, just visible to more than one PID. When the owning test process exits, DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's :DOWN monitor (deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex:241, `handle_info({:DOWN, ...})` -> `owner_down/2`) checks the connection back in and rolls it back -- asynchronously, racing against ExUnit's own on_exit/1 dispatch, with no ordering guarantee between the two.

Concretely, for provision_via_shared_connection/1's own async:false + template::clone default path (the 44-of-47-real-call-sites majority this whole rework exists to keep working): the CREATE SCHEMA / Tenant insert / Registration insert this function performs during the test body live ONLY inside that one sandboxed, rollback-only transaction. By the time on_exit/1 fires (a different process, dispatched after the test process has already exited per §11.10.0's own re-derived ExUnit contract), that transaction has very likely already been rolled back by the :DOWN-triggered automatic checkin -- meaning teardown_wrap's own DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS/delete_all statements, now routed through ProvisioningRepo (a genuinely separate connection/pool), are running against state that was ALREADY GONE before teardown ever touched it, not state teardown itself removes. DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS is silently idempotent against an already-absent schema, and Repo.delete_all against already-absent rows is a silent 0-row no-op, so this produces NO error and NO visible test failure under the ordinary case -- which is exactly why §11.10.2's implementation could look correct (all my new backfill_test.exs assertions genuinely 'pass', because the state really is gone -- just not because of anything teardown_wrap did) while resting on a false premise about durability.

This directly contradicts §11.10.2's own stated safety argument (design doc lines ~3234-3240: 'DataCase's own {:shared, self()}/:auto choice ... never wraps the test body in a transaction that rolls back at teardown; it is a genuine, ordinarily-committing connection ... the same precondition §11.2's own read-your-own-writes argument already rests on'). That claim is checkable against Ecto/DBConnection source and, on direct reproduction, is false: DataCase's checkout is unconditionally a rollback-only sandbox transaction, for every mode. §11.2's own read-your-own-writes argument (why assert_schema_complete!/2 and the test body's OWN later reads see the fixture's writes) is unaffected by this finding -- those reads happen from the SAME process, before it exits, reusing the same still-open transaction, which is exactly right and not in question. What is newly, concretely in question is whether ANYTHING happens after that transaction is gone that still needs the schema/rows to have existed -- and teardown_wrap's whole job is exactly that.

I am stopping here rather than guessing at a fix, per this run's own established discipline (two of my own prior runs on this issue correctly caught real gaps instead of guessing) and per core-directives.md's re-derive rule: this changes the shape of what §11.10 needs to do, not merely a parameter inside it, and a wrong fix here risks masking data durability with an even harder-to-detect failure than the original BLOCKER (a loud exit vs. a silent no-op that happens to look like success). Two observations for whoever re-designs this, offered as evidence, not as a prescribed fix: (1) it is possible the ORIGINAL BLOCKER's own schema/rows were ALSO already gone by the time on_exit fired, pre-§11.10 -- meaning teardown_wrap's connection-usability fix (§11.10.2) may have been necessary but is not sufficient, because a usable connection to run DROP/DELETE against already-vanished state does not, by itself, guarantee the state was ever durable past the owning test's exit; (2) whether this durability gap is actually load-bearing in practice for the 44 async:false callers this rework protects depends on whether their OWN test bodies' assertions (which run before the test process exits, inside the still-open transaction) are the only consumers of the provisioned state -- if so, teardown's own DROP/DELETE may be redundant-but-harmless busywork against already-vanished state today, and the only genuinely open question is whether that remains true for every current and future async:false caller, not just the ones this rework's own regression plan happens to exercise.

All requested implementation work (§11.10.5's three tenant_fixture.ex changes) is done, compiles clean, and is formatted clean. The regression re-run (§11.7 items 1-6) is ALSO fully executed with real quoted output and is reported in issues[] below, including two additional pre-existing, out-of-scope defects found and root-caused during that run (both confirmed via git-worktree bisection against this branch's own pre-fix HEAD, so neither is attributable to this rework): (a) backfill_test.exs's ISS-0343 regression test fails deterministically, at both pre-fix and post-fix HEAD, whenever an async:true TenantFixture caller (secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs) races Backfill.run/1's own unscoped Repo.all(Registration) sweep -- a pre-existing test-isolation gap in that one test's own assertions, unrelated to teardown; (b) test/letflow/api/context_test.exs's two 'byte-identical 404' tests fail deterministically, at both pre-fix and post-fix HEAD, with a Letflow.Repo pool DBConnection.ConnectionError/queue_timeout inside Ecto.Migrator.run/4's own double-checkout requirement -- also pre-existing and unrelated to §11.10. Neither blocks THIS handoff's own verdict but both are real and should be filed as their own issues rather than silently left for the next full-suite TEST-RUNNER gate to rediscover.

issues.description: §11.10.2's core safety premise -- that DataCase's async:false ({:shared, self()}) connection is 'ordinarily-committing, never rolled back at teardown' -- is false, confirmed by direct source read (Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.checkout/2's :sandbox option defaults to true; DataCase never passes sandbox: false; DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's :DOWN monitor rolls the connection back on owner-process exit, per handle_info({:DOWN,...}) at deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex:241) and by a minimal, TenantFixture-free reproduction (a plain DataCase test's CREATE SCHEMA is invisible from a second repo inside on_exit/1, and a direct Letflow.Repo query from on_exit/1 raises DBConnection.OwnershipError: 'cannot find ownership process ... connection's mode reverts to :manual if its owner terminates'). Consequence: provision_via_shared_connection/1's own schema/Tenant/Registration writes for the async:false + template::clone default path may already be rolled back by the time on_exit/1's teardown_wrap runs, making teardown_wrap's own DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS/delete_all statements silent no-ops against already-vanished state rather than the actual cleanup mechanism -- which produces no visible test failure (idempotent DROP, 0-row delete_all) and can look like a passing verification while resting on a false premise. This needs a design-level re-examination of §11.10.2 (ISSUE-FIXER re-diagnosis or CODE-DESIGNER rework), not a code-level patch by ELIXIR-DEV, since it may change what teardown_wrap is even for. Full reproduction steps, source citations, and both observations for the redesign are in this handoff's result.summary.

test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs's pre-existing ISS-0343 regression test ('a tenant whose schema vanished mid-sweep is skipped, not a crash of the whole run') fails deterministically -- assert updated >= 1 gets 0 -- whenever it runs alongside an async:true TenantFixture caller (secrets_test.exs and/or webhooks_test.exs) that happens to be tearing down its own tenant concurrently. Root cause: Backfill.run/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:20) calls Repo.all(Registration) with NO tenant scoping at all -- by design, it sweeps every Registration row in the database -- so under real async concurrency it can pick up an unrelated, concurrently-provisioned-and-torn-down tenant from a DIFFERENT test file, hit that tenant's own 'schema already dropped mid-race' condition, and the reduce_while's own skip-and-continue logic never reaches this test's OWN two tenants at all if timing is unlucky. Confirmed pre-existing via git worktree bisection: identical failure, same assertion, same shape, reproduces at this branch's own pre-fix HEAD (commit 1aa34a9f) with the same async:true+ISS-0343 test combination. Not caused by, or in scope for, this rework's §11.10 changes. Needs its own issue filed against backfill_test.exs's own test isolation (likely fix: scope its own updated/skipped assertions to its own two tenant_ids, or make Backfill.run/1 accept a tenant_id filter for testing).

test/letflow/api/context_test.exs's two 'cross-tenant 404 is byte-identical to a never-existed 404' tests fail deterministically (confirmed across multiple --seed values) with a Letflow.Repo pool DBConnection.ConnectionError (severity: :error, reason: :queue_timeout) raised from inside TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2's own Ecto.Migrator.run/4 call in this test file's own setup block -- 'could not checkout the connection owned by <the test's own PID> ... connections are shared, so this may imply another process is using a connection ... request was dropped from queue after ~500-900ms'. Reproduces in complete isolation (this file alone, no concurrent async files) and confirmed pre-existing via git worktree bisection against this branch's pre-fix HEAD (same two tests fail there too, same error shape, among a larger failure set caused by the still-unfixed BLOCKER at that commit). Root cause appears to be Ecto.Migrator.run/4's own internal need for a second, simultaneous connection while the test process already holds one via the sandbox, colliding with this test's own two provisioned tenants each holding a checkout at setup time -- not anything §11.10 touches (this specific setup block calls TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 directly, never through provision_wrap/teardown_wrap). Needs its own issue filed; not blocking for this handoff.

result.next_action: ORCH: route to ISSUE-FIXER (or CODE-DESIGNER directly, ORCH's call) for a fresh diagnosis of the BLOCKER issue above -- whether provision_via_shared_connection/1's provisioned state genuinely fails to survive to on_exit/1 in practice for real call sites (not just this diagnostic), and if so what the correct fix shape is (a real solution likely needs the schema/rows durable past test-process-exit some other way, or an explicit acceptance that teardown is redundant-but-harmless for this path and the real cleanup is Sandbox's own automatic rollback -- a materially different design position than §11.10.2 currently states). Do NOT route straight to SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER on the current §11.10.5 code -- the three signature-level changes I made match the design exactly and are not themselves wrong, but they may not be doing what the design believes they do, so a security/idiom review of them alone would not catch this. File ISS-0343/context_test.exs's two MAJOR findings as separate, non-blocking issues for a future run per this run's own scope discipline (not this rework's territory).
